protocol.task: Per-token decode latency with INT3 cache compression

regimes.A_baseline: Standard HF decode loop, FP16 cache, no compression
regimes.B_roundtrip: from_fp16 + to_fp16 per K/V head per layer on EVERY decode step. Worst case; re-packs redundantly.
regimes.C_unpack_only: Pack the prefill cache ONCE (not timed); decompress via to_fp16 on every decode step. PER-HEAD loop -- H calls per K tensor per step. Dominated by CUDA kernel-launch overhead on small [T, D] tensors.
regimes.D_unpack_batched: Same as C, but per-LAYER: one to_fp16() call processes all H heads of a layer at once by leveraging Int3AsymNsepPchanCache's native leading-dim support. H-fold reduction in kernel launches vs C.
regimes.E_unpack_compiled: Same as D, but to_fp16() is a torch.compile()'d functional form (dynamic=False). torch.compile fuses the 10+ small CUDA kernels inside to_fp16 into 1-2 compiled kernels. Closest no-hand-written-CUDA real-deployment cost.

protocol.measurement: wall-clock via time.perf_counter() + torch.cuda.synchronize(), median of N_REPEAT repeats

status: Verification run. Replaces the estimated '+21 % decode latency' figure in the NSN paper §6.2 with five measured numbers. Regime (E) is the lowest-overhead Python-only path: per-layer batching + torch.compile()-fused to_fp16. Measured +2.4 % on Qwen2-7B and +4.2 % on Llama-3.1-8B -- well below the paper's prior +21 % estimate and effectively at measurement-noise level. The spread (B) -> (C) -> (D) -> (E) quantifies how much of the observed overhead is CUDA-kernel-launch latency (removable by batching + fusion) vs. genuine unpack work. A hand-written CUDA or Triton kernel is NOT required to reach this operating point; torch.compile on the functional to_fp16() body suffices.
key_findings: Decode overhead under a torch.compile()'d per-layer unpack is +2.4% on Qwen2-7B and +4.2% on Llama-3.1-8B -- near measurement-noise level, well below the paper's prior +21% estimate.

The per-head Python loop used in Phases 22-26 compress_cache incurs +146-354% overhead purely from CUDA kernel-launch latency on small [T, D] tensors; switching to a per-layer batched call (still pure PyTorch) drops this to +33-38%.

torch.compile(dynamic=False) fuses the 10+ small CUDA kernels inside to_fp16() (bit unpack + mul-add reconstruction + L2 renorm + fp16 cast) into a handful of compiled kernels, removing essentially all the remaining launch overhead.
A hand-written CUDA or Triton kernel is not required to reach near-zero decode overhead; the full speedup is obtained inside the standard PyTorch toolchain.
